A deterministic-sequence selection argument makes this uniform in orientation, permitting an independent Haar projection. For Haar rank \(q_p\), the energy fraction has the exact beta law, so \(A_p=(p/q_p)B_p\) has mean one and variance \(2(p-q_p)/(q_p(p+2))\to0\), independently of \((x_p,\rho_p)\). Hence \(R_pA_p-\rho_p\to0\); tightness of \(\rho_p\) then gives tightness of \(R_p\), and \(R_p-\rho_p\to0\). This proves \(R_p\Rightarrow\nu\). No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: PASS. The source explicitly separates two unsatisfied desiderata: one-rank characterization is moment-free only when the parent radius law is already known, while its conditional-isotropy theorem recovers an arbitrary-tail parent radius only after assuming spectral convergence at every proportional rank. The new theorem removes the extra rank continuum under the same natural ACI structure. This is a motivated structural strengthening, especially for elliptical, symmetry-invariant, and conditionally isotropic models, and it partially resolves the paper's stated arbitrary-tail radius-identification gap without imposing moments. The value is the exact hypothesis reduction and radius-recovery mechanism, not the classical Haar beta identity by itself.
